# Donnelly interpreted house, interior-v1

The optional Mount Dora adapter now supplies an explicit two-floor house interpretation. Select **Donnelly - playable house interpretation** (`presentation=interior-v1`) at Donnelly House. Walk with the standard WASD/arrows or captured touch joystick; use the normal contextual action or E to open a door. The same actor, UI, camera and retained frame clock continue from the town through the front door, parlors, return stair and upper chamber, and back outside. The kitchen outside door has its own real five-tread approach.

This is an approved game-layout interpretation. The private source photograph and [National Register nomination 75000560](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/b9a5d338-3817-43d7-b5a4-78737ba59bde) support the off-center entrance into a front parlor, two front parlors, hipped main roof, subsidiary gables, hexagonal corner turret and two-sided veranda. Neither supplies surveyed interior dimensions. The [original proposal](projects/donnelly-house/plan.json) and its drawings remain design evidence. The separate [resolved record](projects/donnelly-house/resolved-interior-v1.json) records the actual room, opening, stair and roof axes. The private photo is excluded from the repository and distribution.

## Resolved native fit

Coordinates use local nominal metre wall axes with engine origin `(386.5,469.5)`. No character or component is scaled to fit. The nominal main shell is 10×12m; its south wall resolves the previous exterior's 0.2m remainder by extending the shell and corresponding slab to the approved axis. The rear wing is 6×9m. Ground and upper floors are **0.848m** and **2.968m**, with **2.12m** pitch, **0.12m** slabs and 0.16m walls. The reference body is **1.8m high, radius0.23m**; the native goat retains its original size.

The architect chose a 5×4m stair hall, moving the study/chamber C boundary from y8 to y9. Both rooms remain 5×3m. The front parlors and exterior envelope retain their approved bounds. The wider engine-owned return-stair variant has twelve rises of `2.12/12m`, five 0.30m goings in each six-rise flight, 1.20m support widths and turn/west landings. Actual used clear passages are at least0.94m east and1.00m north after the authored guards. Rails sit outside the flight support edges; the inner guard and real slab hole prevent side entry and falls. There is no hidden ramp or stair teleport.

Door axes move along their shared walls to clear the real stair and galleries: the parlor/hall and principal/landing doors use y6.65; dining/chamber D north-hall doors use x6.68; study/chamber C doors use x6.68 at y9. The ground back-hall door uses y6.5. Three constrained corner apertures are0.8m wide (dining/back hall, main/back hall, upper front chamber); other single doors are1.0m. The 1.8m connection between parlors is an open framed aperture. Every hinged insert has2.0m clear height and a1.94m leaf, preserving the old1.65m recipes. Door hand/swing and every remaining axis are explicit in the resolved record.

The five ground principal spaces and service group are connected independently; the optional rear stair reservation becomes a store. Four main upper chambers and the rear chamber have their own landing/corridor doors. The shared bath is reached from the corridor, with linen and a store nearby. The circular upper front window belongs to the actual front-chamber bay. The attached lower/upper hexagonal bays belong to the parlor and principal chamber. The third blind turret drum is decorative.

The main roof is a real native hip shell, with a rear hip and two front gables. Its eave underside matches the ceiling and coherent porch posts/bay bearing. The six-sided turret continues into a six-sided profiled cap. The upper attic envelope is deliberately closed to walking; no playable attic floor or stair is advertised. The trunk and gable workbench fit under the actual roof surfaces. The two decorative attic windows move to local y2.7/y4.3 so their complete openings fit below the front gable. Windows, wall cutouts, floors, roof and supports come from the same assembly.

Furniture uses a few original engine arrangements of ordinary solid parts and existing materials: settees/reading and dining tables, a study desk, cooking/washing/storage anchors, beds and dressing storage. Solids block the body and do not become walkable platforms. Circulation and door motion envelopes remain clear. Furniture labels describe inferred domestic uses, without asserting specific historic occupants or plumbing dates.

## Authority and persistence

`planDonnellyHouse()` compiles native slabs, walls, apertures and hinged leaves through `parts-core`. Its immutable compiled scene remains usable by public parts APIs; detached definitions/documents/part arrays can be inspected without mutating future worlds. Convex hexagonal pieces and the explicit wider tread/rail recipe extend the same authored graph. Static rendering is batched by material and cutaway role; doors retain their native hinge/leaf binding.

The house geometry provider adds height-aware support to the existing supported-walk kernel. Ground and upper slabs can overlap in x/y without changing the actor's retained floor or choosing a slab two metres above/below. Every tread and landing has a stable floor/support identity. A retained partial step preserves its exact 3D travel and random-free confirmed-distance native gait. Full upright body sweeps enforce wall, furniture, door, guard and ceiling clearance. A safe prefix remains usable when lookahead meets an obstruction beyond the current movement budget.

Standard interaction previews/commits own door intent, state and revisions. The host saves a0.42-second animation on the existing frame clock. Rendering and collision use the same interpolated hinge angle. Consecutive sweeps of at most one degree use enclosing corner tangents, so a moving leaf pauses safely before meeting an actor and resumes once clear. Opening from inside a swing can require stepping back; the action explains this. Closing uses the standard conservative complete motion envelope. Native edits and new actions wait for retained steps/moving leaves to finish. Actor resources are never refilled or normalized.

The successor world checkpoint is version2 and includes its exact compiled scene, geometry key and door motions, alongside actors, resources, partial travel and native maps. Its app key is `nautilus-mount-dora-session-v1:interior-v1`. Setup/native gait checkpoints retain the shared versioned protocol. Loads reject malformed fields, stale scene/support identities, counterfeit door bindings and mismatched body/travel atomically. The source, photo-guided-v1 and photo-guided-v2 graph/save identities stay independent; no migration or consumer pin update occurs.

Inside, the existing camera follows the same actor while the renderer hides higher levels/roof and cuts walls to show the active floor. Outside, all hip/turret shells return. This is a presentation cutaway, with full physical walls/ceilings retained. The enclosed attic uses the explicitly conservative `closed-attic-eave-v1` body volume, not pitched-roof locomotion. Other geographic buildings remain closed/unverified. Combat, AI, breaking glass and game adoption remain separate bindings.

## Design assessment

**Accuracy:** the hip/hexagonal massing and room/window relationships are preferable for this house to the earlier gable-only/eight-sided study because they follow the building-specific photo and nomination. Dimensions, finishes, furniture, stairs and unseen rooms remain interpretations. Roof and body dimensions above are authored/code measurements, not measurements of the historic building.

**Efficiency:** one native parts compilation supplies drawing, openings, physical surfaces and interaction identities; the host retains the existing source cache, controller, clock and gait. Static material batches and a closed unplayable attic are preferable here to a second controller, duplicate collision layout or detailed attic simulation. Geometry/object counts can be inspected in the browser receipt; no hardware/FPS benchmark is claimed.

**Narrative:** a comfortable recessed hall, independently accessed chambers, service group and small domestic anchors are preferable for a playable Victorian house. The enlarged hall and store alternative are deliberate game-layout choices. Tinderbox may need a richer attic/fire model later; this profile explicitly refuses to imply one. Earlier profiles remain available for compatibility and comparison.

## Reproduction and review

`node tools/donnelly-interior/plan.mjs --check` checks the resolved record. `node tools/donnelly-interior/route.mjs` proves the complete ordinary walk workflow and all room accesses against the opt-in town runtime. Focused tests cover native compilation, upper/ground identity, full-body clearance, real partial travel, occupied/moving doors, rear steps, malformed/stale saves and transactional native authoring.

The bounded `tools/donnelly-interior/review.mjs` reviews held keyboard input or, with `HOUSE_REVIEW_TOUCH=1`, captured trusted touch and ordinary action taps. It observes actual skinned hoof vertices against the correct slab/tread volumes, and requires every native checkpoint revision/pose and rendered root to match host authority. It checks exact mid-door/mid-stair saves, source/installed runtime bytes, active-level visibility and authoring when applicable. It preserves restart sources and closes its isolated browser/server in `finally`. Inspection-camera massing captures are labelled separately from ordinary camera/input proofs.

The outer `docs/reviews/donnelly-interior/registration.json` binds this delta to reviewed base`41398076ae39915cf833ed31efc610a78ddd3ee8`. Earlier ledgers/source notices remain exact and receive only authenticated preimages. All six shallow CI fetch batches include that immutable base. Final frozen delivery uses the required check, full tests, upstream tests and build; the architect owns review, push/PR and integration. No preview is retained by this builder and no Sites audience is changed.
